source_ref.title_or_campaign: 토스 브랜드 런칭 광고 — 돈의 이동에 자유를
source_ref.production_note: Cinematic 30s brand film. Joseon-era historical figures in traditional Korean court costume riding a customized classic American convertible through a desert highway. Korean warrior hood ornament. Plate: 21-KOR-0802 Unlimited. On-screen copy builds: 돈의 이동에 / 돈의 이동에 자유를 / 이제, 자유롭게 / 토스가 시작합니다.

target_demo: Korean adults 20–40s, digitally native, seeking financial freedom and simplicity
narrative_arc: wide_establishing_open → product_detail → character_reveal → copy_build → brand_declaration → wide_exit_logo

production_signature.signature_note: Desert-highway-as-freedom metaphor anchors open and close. Joseon court figures in a classic American convertible create striking anachronistic contrast. Car customised with Korean cultural badges on grille and a traditional general statue as hood ornament. Subtle handheld shimmer on portrait cuts; wide aerial shots fully locked-off with high drone.

global_layout.layout_note: Copy stagger: left-aligned white sans-serif appears line-by-line across portrait shots, building the tagline incrementally. Wide shots bookend the narrative with pure landscape negative space.

copywriting.copy_strategy: incremental_reveal — tagline builds across multiple shots: first 돈의 이동에 alone, then 자유를 fades in, then new line 이제, 자유롭게, concluding with 토스가 시작합니다 on the wide exit shot

audio.audio_note: Cinematic score with male narrator VO. Whisper raw segments corrected against on-screen captions. One segment (11.41-13.41) whisper hallucinated English — actual audio/caption content is 돈의 이동에.

shots.pose_description: Vehicle tiny in center-road vanishing-point composition; horizon at upper third; sky fills upper half with textured clouds; flat desert extends to all edges.

recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: An extreme wide-angle aerial drone photograph taken from approximately 200 meters altitude looking straight down and slightly forward along a perfectly straight two-lane asphalt highway that bisects a vast flat desert plain into two equal halves, creating a strong geometric vanishing-point perspective composition. At the center of the road, a tiny pale steel-blue classic American convertible automobile is barely visible as a small silhouette, occupying less than two percent of the total frame area, emphasizing the overwhelming and humbling scale of the surrounding landscape. The terrain on both sides of the road is arid desert — characteristic of Mojave or Nevada high desert — covered in sparse brown-grey scrub vegetation, dried short desert bushes, and dry reddish-brown sandy soil with occasional pale stone outcroppings. The road itself is perfectly straight with white broken center-lane markings disappearing into the distance. In the far background, a jagged low mountain range with irregular rocky silhouettes rises against the horizon under the dramatic sky. The upper half of the entire frame is dominated by a dramatic overcast sky featuring dense layered stratocumulus clouds lit diffusely from behind and above, creating a moody silver and dark-grey atmospheric texture with subtle variations of luminosity across the cloud formations. The entire image is graded with a desaturated cinematic color look — earth tones are muted to warm ochre and tan, all saturation is pulled down significantly, the sky is pushed towards cool slate-blue grey, and the road asphalt is rendered as a neutral medium grey. No people are visible at all. The atmosphere is one of vast open emptiness. Shallow depth of atmospheric haze softly reduces contrast in the far distance, creating a natural vignette on the horizon. The composition follows a strict rule-of-thirds layout: the horizon line sits precisely at the upper horizontal third, the road vanishing point sits at the exact center of the frame. The lens appears to be a wide rectilinear drone camera with minimal barrel distortion. The cinematic aspect ratio is 16:9. Road markings create a hypnotic linear rhythm converging on the vanishing point. The feeling evoked is epic desolation, the seductive freedom of an infinite open road stretching forever, sublime scale contrast between human transport and nature, and a sense of understated cinematic grandeur. Shot as the opening frame of a Korean fintech brand commercial campaign about financial freedom and movement, with a signature cinematic grade using slight desaturation, lifted shadow tones, and a subtle warm-to-cool color temperature split between ground and sky. The road surface texture shows fine aggregate and tarmac grain visible in the aerial resolution. The white broken center-lane markings are evenly spaced at regular intervals. Dust raised by the vehicle is visible as a faint plume dissipating in the still desert air. The entire composition breathes with cinematic stillness and the promise of infinite forward motion. The drone camera stabilization creates a perfectly static frame where only the vehicle and clouds move. This is the iconic opening image of the campaign, establishing all the visual and emotional grammar of what follows. The desaturation grade creates a timeless quality, neither clearly contemporary nor historical, a visual liminal space appropriate for a story about transcending the boundaries of financial tradition.

A faint coastal or desert-edge haze softens the mountain silhouette to a warm purple-grey tone. The vehicle's large body mass creates a powerful silhouette against the sunset that communicates premium scale and presence. recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A macro close-up still photograph of the front grille section of a classic American full-size luxury convertible automobile from the late 1960s or early 1970s, its body color a deep rich steel-blue metallic paint. The grille itself consists of fine closely-spaced vertical chrome bars arranged in a precise repeating grid pattern, highly polished and reflecting soft overcast daylight in a cool silver shimmer across their surfaces. The rectangular chrome grille frame forms a solid architectural border around this intricate bar pattern. Decorating and adorning the grille bars are five to six small ornamental souvenir collector pins of various shapes depicting traditional Korean cultural heritage imagery, each carefully affixed to the chrome bars with pin clasps: one approximately circular enamel pin featuring a stylized lotus flower in green and pink with the year 1976 inscribed, one shield-shaped pin depicting a traditional multi-tiered stone pagoda tower in grey and silver enamel, one oval-shaped pin with a white-winged crane bird in flight set against a sky-blue enamel background with a decorative rope border, one roughly triangular or mountain-shaped pin depicting a mountainous landscape in muted grey-brown enamel tones, and one red oval pin featuring Korean script lettering in white. Each pin is approximately two to three centimeters in diameter and adds a personal, curated, and culturally rooted decorative identity to the otherwise mass-produced automotive grille. The rectangular dual-headlight housing with round sealed-beam headlamps is partially visible at the right edge of the frame. The chrome front bumper is just visible at the very bottom of the frame, and a partially visible license plate reads 21 KOR 0802 with the handwritten red script word Unlimited above the numbers. The background behind the car is an out-of-focus overcast sky rendered as smooth shallow-depth-of-field bokeh in pale grey. The overall color grade is cool cinematic with subtle desaturation, neutral highlights, and clean shadow rendering. The image conveys crafted personal cultural identity, the playful and deliberate collision of mid-century American automotive heritage with deeply rooted Korean cultural heritage iconography, and the idea that objects can be claimed and reimagined through cultural expression. Cinematic 16:9 aspect ratio, medium macro lens approximately 85mm equivalent, shot from eye-level slightly below the car's headlight height. The spacing between the chrome bars is approximately one centimeter, allowing partial visibility of the dark space behind the grille. The enamel pins are clearly lovingly collected over time, each representing a different facet of Korean cultural and historical identity, the lotus flower as national floral symbol, the pagoda as architectural heritage, the crane as longevity and grace, the mountain as national landscape identity, the cultural script as linguistic heritage. The combination of these distinctly Korean cultural symbols mounted on a distinctly American mid-century automobile grille makes this an image of cultural appropriation and creative reclamation, a statement that Korean identity can inhabit and transform any context. The chrome surface has a few fine surface micro-scratches consistent with authentic use and age, adding realism and tactile authenticity to the detail shot. The reflective surface of the chrome mirrors a distorted abstract impression of the overcast sky above. The visual density of this close-up rewards extended viewing and repeated frames, serving as a key design element in the broader visual identity of the campaign.

recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A macro close-up photograph of the chest and upper shoulder area of a traditional Korean Joseon-dynasty court official's ceremonial outer robe known as a doryeopo or gwanbok worn during formal court functions. The outer garment is crafted from lustrous richly shimmering emerald-green raw silk fabric smooth and tightly woven with a subtle natural sheen visible in the soft overcast daylight. The entire visible surface of the garment is densely embroidered with a magnificent raised three-dimensional gold-thread motif depicting a coiling dragon, the traditional symbol of royalty and supreme authority in Korean court tradition. The dragon motif fills most of the visible fabric surface its body rendered in intricate satin-stitch embroidery using thick gold metallic thread that creates a pronounced three-dimensional relief texture with visible raised ridges along the dragon spine wings and scales. The individual scale shapes are each a small raised lozenge of gleaming gold thread. Flame and cloud motifs accompany the central dragon figure in the embroidery design. At the upper edge of the visible fabric near the neck a crisp multi-layered white cotton inner collar is just visible neat and precisely folded in the traditional Korean court fashion contrasting cleanly against the vivid green of the outer robe. The subject skin at the lower jaw and chin area is barely faintly visible at the very top edge of the frame anchoring the garment to its wearer. The background behind the figure is completely blurred into a smooth uniform pale blue-white sky bokeh with no detail visible. Shot from slightly below the garment looking upward at approximately a thirty to forty-five degree angle creating a subtly heroic compositional angle that emphasizes the garment visual scale and importance. Soft overcast outdoor natural daylight fills the scene evenly from above with minimal harsh shadows. The color grade preserves the fully natural vivid colors, the emerald green and warm metallic gold are rendered at near-full saturation not desaturated like the landscape shots in the broader campaign. Medium telephoto macro lens at approximately one hundred millimeter equivalent focal length with very shallow depth of field keeps the central embroidery texture razor sharp while the edges of the robe and the background fall gently soft. The image conveys regal historical authority deeply-rooted Korean cultural heritage extraordinary craft and artisanship and the intimate textural beauty of traditional ceremonial dress. The composition is abstract and richly sensory, inviting the viewer to appreciate the artistry of the embroiderer and the cultural weight of the costume. Korean fintech brand commercial cinematic 16:9 detail shot. The three-dimensional raised nature of the embroidery creates complex micro-shadow patterns within the gold thread work as the soft light rakes across the surface at a slight angle. The silk base fabric between the embroidered motifs shows its natural woven structure, a tight plain-weave or twill in the characteristic deep emerald green. The white inner collar shows the careful multi-layer folding technique of traditional Korean court dress construction, with several layers of white cotton visible at the neckline. This detail shot communicates that the campaign invests in authentic, high-quality costume construction rather than theatrical approximations. The depth of the embroidery craftsmanship echoes the depth of Korean cultural heritage being invoked throughout the campaign. The specific choice of a dragon motif, reserved in Joseon society for the highest court ranks, deliberately references the campaign theme of unlocking power and authority over one's financial life.

His head is tilted slightly backward with eyes half-closed and gaze directed upward toward the horizon and sky in a relaxed liberated pose suggesting absolute freedom from constraint and a sense of floating in open space. His right arm extends casually resting along the top of the rear seat back. The camera angle is dramatically low, positioned at approximately wheel level or below, so that the dramatic overcast sky fills almost the entire background of the frame, creating a heroic and aspirational framing with the figure rendered against pure sky. The sky is layered with dynamic moving grey-silver overcast clouds lit from above by diffused daylight, with subtle variations in luminosity and texture across the cloud formations. The color grade is cool cinematic with slight desaturation, the pale blue hanbok as the primary saturated color element in an otherwise muted cool scene. The mood conveys liberation, contemplative freedom, and the pleasurable sensation of the wind and sky overhead while moving freely through open space. Korean fintech commercial cinematic 16:9 low angle portrait shot with dramatic sky background. The powder-blue hanbok color has been specifically chosen to contrast with the darker steel-blue car body while harmonizing with the grey-blue overcast sky, creating a tonal relationship that makes him appear to belong to the open sky rather than the enclosed vehicle. The traditional formal court gat hat on his head reads as a sculptural form against the sky, its circular cylindrical silhouette creating a simple but powerful shape. His posture of leaning back with open body language contrasts directly with the formal upright posture expected in traditional Korean court settings, making the physical liberation visible. The caption text in the lower left is carefully positioned to occupy negative space without overlapping the figure, maintaining compositional clarity. The low-angle perspective creates a feeling that the viewer is looking up at this liberated historical figure with admiration and aspiration. The motion-induced robe movement creates dynamic visual energy even in what is essentially a portrait shot, the silk fabric catching the desert wind and streaming backward in a way that emphasizes speed and freedom.
